Customer to provide expected qps and tail-latency SLOs by 2026-03-05
Schedule pilot run (3 days benchmark) week of 2026-03-09
action_items: Diego Martinez: Upload SOC2 pack & SSO guide - due 2026-03-03
Lena Ortiz: Share example traffic patterns and token distributions - due 2026-03-05

summary: Kickoff and risk alignment for Everbrook Systems onboarding. Covered deployment modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security checklist (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS), expected traffic and latency SLOs, and proposed 3-day pilot. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-27 15:00 PT | Duration: 59m | Attendees: Ava, Priya, Diego (Redwood) — Mark, Lena, Sam (Everbrook)

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro: I'm Ava, I'll run the kickoff and handoff to Diego and Priya for tech details. welcome Everbrook.
[00:18] Mark: Thanks, Ava. Sam and I are here, lena dialed in from platform. excited to get moving. we've got tighter compliance needs so wanted to align on risks early.
[00:35] Diego: great, high level today's goals: confirm success criteria, surface any blockers (security/networking), and agree pilot window.
[00:47] Priya: I will cover the runtime options and what we typically recommend for low-latency vector workloads.
[01:05] Sam: quick background — Everbrook is building an assistive code-review feature, about 120 rps at peak, token sizes avg 700, worst-case 2k. retention rules: keep logs for 90 days, PII scrub on ingest.
[01:30] Priya: ok good, that token distribution pushes us toward a configuration that favors KV cache efficiency and batching — and depending on tolerable tail you'd probably pick dedicated or private.
[01:48] Lena: we prefer VPC peering for now. on-prem is possible but we'd rather start with a VPC/private deployment. SSO is non-negotiable, SOC2 required for our audit.
[02:10] Ava: noted — Diego will share our SOC2 pack, and we support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. we also have KMS integrations for customer-managed keys.
[02:25] Mark: helpful. one ask: can we get a proof that logs are encrypted at rest with customer keys?
[02:33] Diego: yes, we'll include KMS diagrams and HSM notes in the security docs.
[02:40] Priya: about perf — for 120 rps with 700 tokens avg, typical latency on Dedicated is sub-200ms p50 on T4/RTX-class hardware, p95 varies with batching profile. if you need sub-100ms we recommend a smaller batch target and larger reserved capacity.
[03:05] Sam: p95 under 500ms would be acceptable for initial release; long-term goal sub-200ms.
[03:12] Priya: good, that maps. we should still run a 3-day pilot with your exact traffic to validate KV cache hit rates.
[03:24] Mark: yes — what does Redwood need from us to run pilot?
[03:29] Priya: token distribution, qps per endpoint, sample prompts (we can sanitize), plus an account to push test traffic — we can also run pass-through with live traffic if you prefer.
[03:45] Lena: we'll share sanitized traffic and a redacted dataset. also need details on egress and network rules for the VPC peering.
[03:55] Ava: we'll send a VPC checklist and firewall rules.
[04:05] (ambient note: brief crosstalk, someone on airport wifi)
[04:30] Priya: security deep-dive quick: for Private deployment we do a lightweight control plane in our cloud, customer data plane sits in your VPC or on-prem. if you want fully air-gapped, that requires our private package and a support SLA change.
[04:55] Sam: budget question — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
[05:02] Diego: short answer: hosted is lower up-front, but with your volume dedicated gives predictable unit economics and better p95. i'll follow up with a tailored cost model.
[05:14] Sam: perfect. competitor question: how do you compare vs Anthropic/OpenAI for cost/latency and auditability?
[05:22] Ava: we position for production economics — we publish benchmark profiles by model, and give controls like quantization, batching, caching, router policies. for auditability we provide audit logs, KMS, SOC2 and contract terms for data residency.
[05:40] Mark: about audit logs — retention 90 days, can we hook logs to our SIEM?
[05:47] Diego: yes, we support push to your S3 or syslog collector with encryption.
[06:00] (longer technical exchange between Priya and Lena about tokenization, early truncation strategies)
[10:22] Priya: small note on evals: bring a representative prompt set so our quality team can run regression checks when we suggest quantization or smaller model variants.
[10:45] Mark: we'll do that.
[15:00] Priya: network requirements — you'll need an outbound to our control plane endpoints, and a peering link for data plane if using private. firewall rules will be in the checklist.
[20:10] (customer asks for SLA language)
[20:20] Ava: our Dedicated contracts include uptime and latency targets; for legal we'd surface sample SLA language. Diego will coordinate procurement touchpoints.
[25:35] Sam: procurement timeline — we want legal/ procurement to wrap in 6 weeks ideally.
[25:45] Diego: noted; i'll flag that in the CRM.
[30:00] (discussion about internal teams, who owns day-to-day ops at Everbrook)
[32:12] Lena: we'll have two owners — infra (me) and ML ops (Mark). for runbooks, can Redwood provide standard incident runbooks?
[32:24] Diego: yes, runbooks + playbooks for common incidents (KV cache miss storms, disk pressure, degraded models). we'll attach examples.
[36:40] Priya: pilot config suggestion: 3-day run, 1% live traffic (shadowed) day 1, 10% day 2, full synthetic load mapped to your patterns day 3. during this time we'll capture p50/p90/p95 and token costs.
[37:05] Mark: timeline works. who will run the pilot?
[37:10] Ava: Redwood ops + Priya for instrumentation, you provide traffic and credentials for staging. Diego will be PM for docs and procurement.
[38:00] (brief pause)
[38:12] Sam: security follow-ups: can you provide penetration test summary and your third-party infra list?
[38:20] Diego: yes — pentest summary + cloud provider inventory will be in the SOC2 pack.
[40:00] (question about data residency in EU)
[40:08] Mark: some of our customers are EU-based; will Redwood guarantee region placement?
[40:14] Ava: yes, we can pin model serving to EU region with Private or Dedicated capacity; will include region routing in the rollout plan.
[42:33] Priya: operational note: for model updates we'll support canary rollouts and auto-fallback to previous variant if quality drops. we'll entitle you to a model-version pinning process.
[45:00] Lena: great. also need RBAC for our teams.
[45:06] Diego: we support RBAC and team scoping — we'll send example roles.
[50:12] (wrap-up) Ava: recap: we will share SOC2 + SSO + KMS docs (Diego), Pilot plan + Dedicated vs Hosted cost sheet (Priya), Everbrook to send traffic patterns and example prompts (Lena/Mark). agreed pilot 3-day window week of Mar 9.
[50:35] Sam: ok, thanks. one ask — can we get a simplified runbook for on-call folks?
[50:42] Diego: yes, short runbook will be in the handoff bundle.
[51:00] (closing pleasantries)
[51:12] Ava: i'll follow up with calendar invites and links to the shared drive. Diego will open a ticket in CRM with attachments.
[51:30] Mark: thanks everyone, looking forward.

Action items (spoken in call):
- Diego Martinez: Share SOC2 pack & SAML/SCIM integration guide by 2026-03-03
- Priya Kapoor: Produce Dedicated vs Hosted cost/latency comparison and pilot config by 2026-03-04
- Lena Ortiz: Provide sanitized traffic logs and token distribution by 2026-03-05
- Diego Martinez: Create CRM deal folder and attach security artifacts by 2026-03-03

References shared: Redwood onboarding checklist (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboard/everbrook), Pilot template spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/pilots/everbrook-template), SOC2 summary (to be attached).

End of transcript.
